summary: Gemfibrozil is a fibrate used as adjunct to diet for very high triglycerides (Types IV/V) with pancreatitis risk, and to reduce coronary heart disease risk in select Type IIb patients who have not responded to other measures. It lowers triglycerides/VLDL and raises HDL. Key cautions: increased risk of gallstones and of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis (markedly so with statins - combination with simvastatin is contraindicated), and it is contraindicated in hepatic or severe renal dysfunction. It strongly inhibits drug clearance via OATP1B1/CYP2C8/glucuronidation, contraindicating combination with repaglinide, dasabuvir, and selexipag.
indications: Adjunct to diet for very high serum triglycerides (Types IV and V hyperlipidemia) at risk of pancreatitis, not responding to diet
Reducing coronary heart disease risk in Type IIb patients without history/symptoms of CHD who have not responded to diet, weight loss, exercise, and other lipid drugs

moa: Fibric acid derivative (PPAR-alpha agonist) that decreases hepatic VLDL triglyceride production and increases lipoprotein lipase activity, lowering serum triglycerides and VLDL cholesterol; it also raises HDL cholesterol (HDL2, HDL3, apo AI/AII). Effects on LDL are variable.

absolute: Hepatic dysfunction including primary biliary cirrhosis

preg: Limited human data; use only if clearly needed and potential benefit justifies risk (historically pregnancy category C).
lact: Unknown whether excreted in human milk; because of potential for tumorigenicity seen in animals, decide whether to discontinue nursing or the drug.
renal: Contraindicated in severe renal dysfunction; use caution with mild-to-moderate impairment (increased myopathy risk; consider dose reduction or avoid).
hepatic: Contraindicated in hepatic dysfunction and primary biliary cirrhosis; monitor liver function and discontinue if abnormalities persist.

major: Simvastatin (contraindicated) and other statins - markedly increased rhabdomyolysis/myopathy risk
Repaglinide (contraindicated) - severe hypoglycemia from CYP2C8/OATP1B1 inhibition
moderate: Other CYP2C8/OATP1B1 substrates (e.g., loperamide, paclitaxel, montelukast) - increased levels
Colestipol/bile acid sequestrants - reduce gemfibrozil absorption (separate dosing)
interactions.food: Take 30 minutes before meals; food reduces absorption if taken with meals
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol - raises triglycerides and hepatic risk
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor LFTs and CBC; check CK if muscle symptoms; reduce/hold interacting drug doses.

Muscle symptoms; creatine kinase if myopathy suspected
Blood glucose (when combined with antidiabetic agents)
counsel: Take 30 minutes before your morning and evening meals

pearls: Combination with simvastatin, repaglinide, dasabuvir, and selexipag is contraindicated
Markedly increases myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk with any statin - avoid or minimize
Increases gallstone formation - like clofibrate (lithogenic bile)
Best for very high triglycerides and pancreatitis prevention; effect on LDL is variable
Inhibits OATP1B1, CYP2C8, and glucuronidation - many drug interactions
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered before a meal; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Reported overdoses caused abdominal cramps, abnormal LFTs, diarrhea, increased CK, joint/muscle pain, nausea, and vomiting. There is no specific antidote; provide symptomatic and supportive care.
